_comment: Which Factorio version each fixture's ground truth was captured from.
This lives beside the fixtures rather than inside them because several are
verbatim copies of the game's own JSON structures (autoplace-can-be-disabled
is a flat dict keyed by control name, asserted key-for-key in catalog.spec.ts),
so an added metadata key would be data pollution, not annotation.
'evidence' grades how the version was established - 'inferred' is weaker than
'stated', and 'unknown' means nobody wrote it down. Do not upgrade an inferred
or unknown entry without re-capturing against a known binary.
Every file in this directory is named, either in 'fixtures' or, when it is
deliberately not ground truth, in 'notFixtures' with a reason. The check used
to glob '.json' and '.png', and eight captured map exchange strings sat
unrecorded behind that filter for a month (issue #240). Filtering by extension
is how ground truth goes unrecorded, so there is no longer a filter.
'maxUnknown' is the ratchet. The number of 'unknown' entries must EQUAL it, so
adding one fails, and resolving one fails until the number is lowered - the old
less-than-or-equal bound never had to fall.
Enforced by test/fixtureProvenance.spec.ts; report staleness with

oracle-fulgora-cells.seed123456.json.evidence: captured 2026-08-13 via test/oracle/capture.ts fulgora-cells against a real Fulgora surface on the installed 2.1.14 (build 87180) binary; the map-gen Lua it ports is byte-identical 2.1.12 -> 2.1.14. Positions are IDENTICAL to oracle-fulgora-shared.seed123456.json, so the two fixtures line up index-for-index and the spec asserts that. Also carries `gridSizeProbe`, which answers a question the default settings cannot: `grid_size` is documented as a 16-bit UNSIGNED INTEGER but `fulgora_grid` is a genuine float away from the two slider endpoints, so does the voronoi call truncate? The probe samples voronoi_cell_id at a FRACTIONAL grid_size of 155.65736389160156 - what fulgora_grid really is at islands frequency 2 - against the two integers it sits between, 155 and 156. Result: fractional matches truncated 101/101 and rounded only 91/101, and the 10 positions where 155 and 156 disagree are what make it a measurement rather than a coincidence. The default grid is exactly 175, which is why a literal was needed.

oracle-fulgora-elevation.seed123456.json.evidence: captured 2026-08-13 via test/oracle/capture.ts fulgora-elevation against a real Fulgora surface on the installed 2.1.14 (build 87180) binary; the map-gen Lua it ports is byte-identical 2.1.12 -> 2.1.14. Positions are IDENTICAL to oracle-fulgora-shared and oracle-fulgora-cells, so all three fixtures line up index-for-index and the spec asserts it. Carries the five multioctave sources plus every named expression from fulgora_natural through fulgora_elevation, including the two INTERNAL nodes (fulgora_vault_pyramids_and_start, fulgora_pre_elevation) that nothing else consumes - captured so a transcription error in either localises instead of arriving blended into elevation. Also carries `sliderRescaleProbe`, which answers a question the captured positions cannot: fulgora_natural scales by slider_rescale(control:fulgora_islands:size, 2), and at the DEFAULT size slider of 1 that is 2^0 = 1 exactly, so every one of the 101 positions is blind to how the game evaluates it. The probe samples slider_rescale(s, 2) at literal s of 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6. Result: f32 per-operation rounding matches all 7 exactly, an f64 chain rounded once at the end misses s=0.5 and s=5 by one ulp, and the noise machine's fastapprox pow misses 6 of 7 - so the function is exact math, evaluated per-operation at f32, the same shape already measured for slider_to_linear.

oracle-fulgora-ruins.seed123456.json.evidence: captured 2026-08-13 and EXTENDED 2026-08-14 via test/oracle/capture.ts fulgora-ruins against a real Fulgora surface (game.planets['fulgora'].create_surface()) on the installed 2.1.14 binary, which pnpm refs:sync --check reported in sync at both capture times. Positions are identical to oracle-fulgora-shared/cells/elevation.seed123456.json, so all four line up index-for-index. 26 fields. 22 are named expressions: the three masks, the road and structure layer including its intermediate paving stages, and the ruins layer with its four tile_ruin outputs. The other 4 (fulgoran_dust/dunes/sand/rock_probability) are the COMPOSITE probability_expressions of the four land tiles that declare no named expression of their own, sampled as the verbatim strings from tiles-fulgora.lua lines 293/330/367/404 - the harness registers any expression string as a noise-expression prototype, so the game does the parsing. The 2026-08-14 recapture reproduced all 22 original fields BIT-IDENTICALLY (checked field-by-field against the committed values, not assumed), which re-validates the whole fixture against the current binary rather than only adding to it.

oracle-fulgora-tiles.seed123456.json.evidence: captured 2026-08-13 via test/oracle/capture.ts fulgora-tiles against a real Fulgora surface on the installed 2.1.14 (build 87180) binary. This is surface.get_tile(x, y).name after real chunk generation - the tile the game actually PLACED, not a noise value, so it is the only fixture in the Fulgora set that can check the autoplace argmax rather than an expression. 5057 points in two samples: a contiguous 256x256 block at stride 4 centred on (-1500, 1000), plus a coarse stride-400 grid to +/-6000 tiles. The block centre was chosen by asking the PORT for the 256x256 block nearest a 50/50 oil-mask split, so the sample is deliberately concentrated on the coastline rather than on convenient interior; the block's own mixedness is then asserted from the GAME's names, so the port's choice cannot make the check vacuous. Result: 2796 ocean tiles (deep 1136, shallow-2 694, shallow 508, deep-2 458) and 2261 land (paving 685, rock 493, walls 269, dust 224, dunes 219, conduit 147, sand 116, machinery 108). positions are the mod's ECHOED floored get_tile input, so a caller cannot pair an unfloored position with a floored sample.

oracle-fulgora-scrap.seed123456.json.evidence: captured 2026-08-14 via test/oracle/capture.ts fulgora-scrap against a real Fulgora surface (game.planets['fulgora'].create_surface(), seed FORCED to 123456) on the installed 2.1.14 (build 87180) binary, which pnpm refs:sync --check reported in sync at capture time. Carries scrap's probability_expression with its local_expressions inlined (STRUCT and VAULT terms), the two terms individually, and the two control levers (scrap frequency and size) read back at their default value of 1. Every FIELD the expression reads (fulgora_structure_cells, fulgora_structure_subnoise, fulgora_elevation, fulgora_coastline, fulgora_artificial_mask, fulgora_spots_prebanding, fulgora_vaults_and_starting_vault, fulgora_starting_mask, fulgora_road_paving_2c) is already covered by the shared/cells/elevation/ruins fixtures at the same 101 positions, so this fixture covers only the COMPOSITION - operator precedence and the two mins. Result: fulgora_scrap_probability spans 0 to the 0.5 cap across the 101 positions (2 of 101 nonzero), so the sample is not vacuous against a stub that always returns 0.

oracle-fulgora-scrap-entities.seed123456.evidence: captured 2026-08-14 via test/oracle/capture.ts fulgora-scrap-entities against a real Fulgora surface (game.planets['fulgora'].create_surface(), seed FORCED to 123456) on the installed 2.1.14 (build 87180) binary, which pnpm refs:sync --check reported in sync at capture time. Three regions, chunk-forced generation, find_entities_filtered{type='resource'} at the DEFAULT preset: [0,0]-[256,256] found 222 scrap, [-1200,800]-[-944,1056] found 191, [800,-1600]-[1056,-1344] found 149. `protos.scrap` records the collision box, cliff_removal_probability and map_grid read off the running game (map_grid: true, as expected for a non-fluid, non-vent resource). This is the DENSITY oracle; the preview PNGs cannot substitute for it because ResourceEntityPrototype::map_grid defaults to true, so the game's map preview draws solid ore as a 2x2-tile checkerboard and shows about 0.5 pixels per entity.

oracle-fulgora-shared.seed123456.json.evidence: captured 2026-08-13 via test/oracle/capture.ts fulgora-shared against a real Fulgora surface (game.planets['fulgora'].create_surface()) on the installed 2.1.14 (build 87180) binary, which pnpm refs:sync --check reported in sync at capture time. The map-gen Lua it ports is byte-identical 2.1.12 -> 2.1.14 (empty git diff over space-age/prototypes/planet/, noise-programs.lua, noise-functions.lua and base noise-expressions.lua), so this is 2.1.14 ground truth for a subsystem that did not move. 101 positions spanning BOTH scales on purpose: a 7x7 sweep across one 175-tile grid cell plus six far-field rings out to r=15000. The two scales test different things - the starting cones are non-zero at only 30 and 16 of the 101 positions, all near spawn, while the far rings are what exercise the wobble octaves - so a near-only or far-only capture would let a wrong input_scale or an unevaluated cone pass.

oracle-vulcanus-cliff-suppressor-levers..evidence:
captured 2026-08-03 by test/oracle/capture.ts vulcanus-cliff-suppressor-levers against the installed binary, which pnpm refs:sync --check reported in sync at 2.1.12 at capture time. Five arms over [1500,1500] that pull two LEVERS through map_gen_settings.autoplace_settings rather than modelling a suppressor: the whole entity category off (treat_missing_as_default = false, no settings), and lava/lava-hot dropped from the tile category while every other tile is kept. Each arm reads the autoplace_settings the SURFACE reported back AND counts the lava tiles in the region it just generated, so an override that failed to apply cannot pass as a term that does not matter; the two entity-lever arms additionally dump EVERY entity in the region with its type, and every arm dumps the prototype collision geometry, all from ONE generated surface.

oracle-voronoi-cellid.multiseed.json.evidence: stated - captured 2026-08-04 by test/oracle/capture.ts voronoi-cellid against the installed binary, which pnpm refs:sync --check reported in sync at 2.1.12 at capture time. voronoi_cell_id sampled at cell centres across 3 seed0 x 3 seed1: seed0 (the map seed) in [123456, 1, 4294967295], seed1 in [0, 1, 137], at grid_size 64 and jitter 0, routed onto elevation on the default Nauvis surface. cell_id is the per-cell RNG exposed directly as a float, so this is the hash with no geometry in the way; a cell centre gives one value per cell with no boundary ambiguity, and distance_type does not enter it at all (oracle-voronoi-jitter0 asserts all four distance types agree value-for-value), so only chebyshev is sampled. The four voronoi_* ops x the four distance_type values at JITTER 0, where every point sits at its cell centre and the per-cell RNG moves nothing, so the ops reduce to pure geometry. FIFTEEN series, not sixteen: the game's own noise-expression compiler rejects voronoi_pyramid_noise x minkowski3 outright ('Voronoi pyramid noise with Minkowski3 distance is not supported'), measured by compiling all 16 pairs - the other 15 reach on_init. oracle-voronoi-points.seed123456.json.evidence: stated - captured 2026-08-05 by test/oracle/capture.ts voronoi-points against the installed binary, which pnpm refs:sync --check reported in sync at 2.1.12 at capture time. JITTERED voronoi point placement at jitter 0.6 / 0.8 / 1.0, grid_size 64, seed0 123456, seed1 1, routed onto elevation on the default Nauvis surface (voronoi_* are engine builtins, not planet-scoped, so no Space Age load is involved). TWO readouts. `series` is the inversion lattice: voronoi_spot_noise plus voronoi_cell_id over the 64x64 tile centres of cell (3,5), under manhattan and euclidean. spot_noise is a cone whose apex sits ON the point, so its minimum over the lattice recovers the point with no model in the loop; the lattice covers the WHOLE cell rather than a neighbourhood of a predicted position, because at jitter 1 the point may be anywhere in the cell and a lattice built around a prediction could only confirm that prediction. cell_id is captured at the same positions and is not redundant: spot_noise is the distance to the nearest point of ANY cell, so a neighbour's point just outside the boundary can win the global argmin, and cell_id says which cell owns each lattice position so the argmin can be restricted to the ones this cell actually owns. `ops` is the exact-f32 acceptance set: the same 15 op x distance_type series and the same 175 positions as oracle-voronoi-jitter0, re-captured at each of the three jitters (45 series). Fifteen and not sixteen for the same reason as that fixture - the game's compiler rejects voronoi_pyramid_noise x minkowski3. Every lattice coordinate is a multiple of 1/2 a tile and therefore exact in the 1/256 MapPosition grid whatever its sign, so no rounding rule applies to the probe positions at all; test/oracle/capture.ts asserts that rather than snapping.

oracle-voronoi-search-range.seed123456.j.evidence: stated - captured 2026-08-05 by test/oracle/capture.ts voronoi-search-range against the installed binary, which pnpm refs:sync --check reported in sync at 2.1.12 at capture time. voronoi_pyramid_noise routed onto elevation on the default Nauvis surface (voronoi_* are engine builtins, not planet-scoped, so no Space Age load is involved), grid_size 64, seed0 123456, seed1 1. These are the ONLY positions in the repo where the game's own VoronoiNoise::getPointsSearchRange() is observable: a 3x3 and a 5x5 cell search give different answers there. The other two voronoi fixtures are indifferent to it in BOTH directions - forcing the port's range to 1, and to 2, each passed all 95 voronoi tests over their 2100 values - and Factorio changed this behaviour in 2.1.7 (forums.factorio.com/130905), so without these the skew would be silent. Only voronoi_pyramid_noise can discriminate: spot/facet/cell_id reduce to the two smallest point distances and a ring-2 point is over a grid unit away on one axis, while the pyramid minimises the distance to each pair's BISECTOR, which is small whenever a far point is nearly EQUIDISTANT rather than nearer. Five series pin both branches: chebyshev at jitter 1 (the table's pinned 1, and Fulgora's fulgora_road_pyramids configuration), manhattan and euclidean at jitter 1 (the '> threshold ? 2' branch), and manhattan 0.7 / euclidean 0.9, the lowest jitters found to discriminate at all, which bound those thresholds from above. Positions were located by sweeping the PORT with the ring forced to each value and keeping samples that differ by more than 2%, thinned by a stride so they are not one cluster; the port chooses only where to look and the game alone says which answer is right. Every coordinate is a multiple of 1/2 a tile and therefore exact in the 1/256 MapPosition grid whatever its sign; capture.ts asserts that rather than snapping.

oracle-fastpow.seed123456.json.evidence: stated - captured 2026-08-05 by test/oracle/capture.ts fastpow against the installed binary (2.1.12, build 87038), which pnpm refs:sync --check reported in sync at capture time. Note 2.1.13 released the same day; its changelog contains no map-generation, noise, terrain, autoplace, cliff or map-exchange entries. The probe samples the noise machine's own `^` operator as `x ^ <exponent>` routed onto elevation on the default Nauvis surface, so fastApprox is compared to the operator DIRECTLY rather than through a downstream chain - every other fixture over fastApprox compares with a tolerance wide enough to hide the ~1e-5 effects at issue (#161, #162). Four series: 1/3 (the shipping cube root), 0.5, 2.5 and 2. The exponents are not interchangeable and the fixture is what established that: `^` has THREE behaviours, all at 123/123 - 1/3 and 2.5 reach Math::powSafe(float,float) and so the fastapprox log2/exp2 pair; 0.5 is an exact sqrt; an integral exponent takes powSafe's fcvtzs/scvtf fast path and is exact exponentiation by squaring. The 0.5 result was a refutation - the spec first asserted fastapprox there and the game disagreed at the first position. Positions are deliberately adversarial rather than a plain grid, which does not discriminate (12 evenly spaced points scored 12/12 for both candidate cube-root exponents): they include 24 points where a double 1/3 differs from f32(1/3), which settled #163 at 0/24 against 24/24, and points where the pre-9b49ebb single-rounding fastapprox differs from the per-operation rounding that replaced it (~30% of inputs). Every coordinate is a multiple of 1/2 a tile and therefore exact in the 1/256 MapPosition grid.

notFixtures.wasm-request.v2.json: not Factorio ground truth, so it has no game version to record - it pins OUR OWN WASM request encoding at ABI v2 (#225, replacing the v1 entry from #223), whose layout tables live in crates/fmw-wasm/src/abi.rs. It is read by a spec, unlike most entries here: test/wasmFulgoraRenderParity.spec.ts asserts the TypeScript writer produces exactly these bytes for both a Fulgora and a Vulcanus request, so neither side of the boundary can move a field without the other going red. The bytes were checked by test/fixtures/verify-wasm-request.py, a third implementation written from the layout table, rather than by re-running the writer - which would only have proved the writer agrees with itself.
notFixtures.verify-wasm-request.py: a tool, not ground truth. It is the independent decoder that verified wasm-request.v2.json, committed beside it so a future ABI version can be re-verified the same way rather than by regenerating the bytes from the encoder under test. It deliberately does not reproduce the trig VALUES - those are V8's Math.sin after an f32 narrowing, and a second libm is exactly the disagreement #270 measured - so it checks the trig block structurally: unit norm per pair, one legitimate duplicate, and each bearing's angle recovered with atan2 and checked against the offset the game's Lua gives it. Seven planted breaks were confirmed caught, including two bearing swaps that the unit-norm check alone was measured MISSING. The cliff cell query box (#225, ABI v2's Vulcanus block growing 248 -> 280 bytes with no version bump) added FIVE more, all confirmed caught by its per-edge value check: a transposed x0/x1, four identical edges, a block shifted by one f64, a mismatched y0, and a declared length still saying 248. Its two structural checks - four distinct edges, not inverted on either axis - constrain the FIXTURE rather than catching a break, and the file says so rather than claiming credit for the five.
